# Results — Study 688 (Concealing Baby Swallow)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — the
**concealing baby swallow**, a four-candle bullish reversal from the candlestick canon:
two black marubozu, a black candle that gaps down then rallies into the prior body before
closing low, and a fourth black candle that totally engulfs the third yet closes at a new
low — the "capitulation" that supposedly ends a downtrend. Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30**
(the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint
`d60f851e5d11` (basket close panel, 111 tickers, 1,248,608 rows).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV, **111 tickers** — SPY, QQQ, DIA, IWM + 107 long-listed US large-caps across every major sector — cache-first, 1962-01-02 → 2026-06-30 |
| Coverage | **4,957 name-years** searched; longest single series (XOM, JNJ, PG, KO, IBM, …) spans **64.5 years**; every bar of every ticker is scanned |
| Detector | two cuts — **loose** (plain geometric reading: marubozu + downtrend + day-3 overlap-then-fail + day-4 full engulf) and **strict** (literature-close: true marubozu, true gap-downs, day-4 opens inside day-3's shadow) |
| Statistics | Welch *t* (reversal vs base rate) and one-sample HAC *t*, **only computed above the pre-registered floor `MIN_N_FOR_TEST = 8` pooled events**; Bonferroni-corrected critical \|*t*\| = **2.50** for 4 simultaneous horizons where a test *does* run |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: enter the next session's **open** after the confirming (day-4) close — one execution lag, no look-ahead; long-only, no borrow |
| Data quirks (named) | one of the four loose-cut hits (GD, 1962-06-14) prints at a split-adjusted price near **$0.12/share** — coarse penny-level rounding at that price level can manufacture near-zero-shadow ("marubozu") geometry on its own; flagged, not excluded |

No survivorship weighting inside a single event study, but the basket itself is a
**survivors** panel (all 111 names trade today) — named on the Signal axis. For a rare,
single-pattern event count this affects *which names* could contribute a candidate, not
the direction of any comparison made.

## The search — scanning every bar of every ticker for the four-candle shape

| cut | occurrences | vs the pre-registered floor |
|---|--:|---|
| loose (plain geometric reading) | **4** | below `MIN_N_FOR_TEST = 8` — **no *t*-statistic computed** |
| strict (literature-close) | **0** | below `MIN_N_FOR_TEST = 8` — **no *t*-statistic computed** |

Across the desk's largest single-pattern basket (111 tickers) and longest single-pattern
history (up to 64.5 years, 4,957 name-years total), the plain reading of the pattern
fires **four times**, ever. The literature-close cut — true marubozu, a true gap down on
day 3, day 4 opening inside day 3's shadow — fires **zero** times. This is not a
disappointing result of the test; it *is* the result: the pattern, as literally defined,
is too rare to expose to disconfirming evidence at any practical sample size.

### Every loose-cut occurrence found, in full

| ticker | day-4 confirms | strict? | fwd 1d | fwd 5d | fwd 10d | fwd 20d |
|---|---|:--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| GD | 1962-06-14 | no | +404.6 bp | −404.6 bp | +867.1 bp | +867.1 bp |
| BDX | 1993-01-06 | no | +97.4 bp | +32.5 bp | −64.9 bp | +340.9 bp |
| CL | 2004-09-23 | no | −148.4 bp | −141.8 bp | −309.8 bp | +57.6 bp |
| KMI | 2011-08-22 | no | +254.9 bp | +576.7 bp | +601.8 bp | +1,157.5 bp |
| **mean (n=4, untested)** | | | **+152.1 bp** | **+15.7 bp** | **+273.5 bp** | **+605.8 bp** |

Four points, no consistent sign across horizons (the 5-day column is roughly flat, the
20-day column looks impressive because one observation — KMI, +11.6% — dominates a
four-point mean). **`GD` (1962-06-14) trades at a split-adjusted ~$0.12/share** — 1960s
tick sizes at that price level are coarse enough that near-zero-shadow geometry can be a
rounding artifact rather than genuine one-way selling; the other three occurrences sit at
ordinary modern-era prices. None of the four is a *strict* occurrence.

## Context — the base rate (same long bet on every 4-red-days-in-a-downtrend bar)

The unconditional base rate answers "what does buying the next open after **any** four
consecutive red closes in a downtrend earn?", isolating the pattern's own claimed
information from plain downtrend mean reversion. It is enormous — the coarse shape
("four reds in a downtrend") is common — and has its own strong, HAC-significant positive
drift, which is simply the well-known short-horizon bounce after a decline (not evidence
for or against the concealing-baby-swallow claim):

| horizon | base-rate *n* | base-rate mean | base-rate HAC *t* | the 4 CBS occurrences mean | CBS *n* (untested) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1d | 31,552 | +10.8 bp | +7.74 | +152.1 bp | 4 |
| 5d | 31,528 | +85.7 bp | +19.97 | +15.7 bp | 4 |
| 10d | 31,516 | +126.2 bp | +19.73 | +273.5 bp | 4 |
| 20d | 31,491 | +220.3 bp | +22.55 | +605.8 bp | 4 |

The delta (CBS mean − base-rate mean) swings from −70.0 bp (5d) to +385.5 bp (20d) —
exactly the kind of noisy, sign-flipping pattern four independent draws produce. **No
Welch *t* is reported for any horizon**: `strategy.welch_t` returns `None`, by
construction, whenever either side has fewer than 8 finite observations, and here the CBS
side always has exactly 4.

## Descriptive-only placebo (not a certifying test)

For transparency only — never cited as evidence — a label-shuffle placebo draws 4 random
"four-red-days-in-a-downtrend" bars from the base-rate pool, 2,000 times, and asks how
often the random draw's mean beats the observed CBS mean:

| horizon | observed mean | placebo mean (2,000 draws of 4) | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1d | +152.1 bp | +9.7 bp | 0.084 |
| 5d | +15.7 bp | +81.1 bp | 0.615 |
| 10d | +273.5 bp | +122.7 bp | 0.305 |
| 20d | +605.8 bp | +237.3 bp | 0.193 |

None of the four horizons is remotely significant even by this generous, unpenalized
read (and 4-vs-4 Bonferroni-style correction for 4 horizons would need *p* < 0.0125).
This is decoration on top of an already-untested sample, printed only so nobody wonders
whether we quietly ran the test and hid it.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic panel with a controlled rate of engineered four-candle blocks (exact
marubozu / gap-rally-fail / full-engulf geometry) and a tunable planted post-pattern
bounce (`edge`); no network.

| world | *n* events found | Welch *t* (reversal vs base) |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | 422 – 494 per seed | mean **+0.68** (sd 0.95), \|*t*\| ≥ 2 in **1/20** seeds |
| planted `edge = +0.05` (seed 688) | 456 | **+14.39** |

The null's 1-in-20 firing rate matches the *nominal* two-sided 5% false-positive rate of
a |*t*| ≥ 2 threshold almost exactly — there is no systematic bias toward finding
significance in noise. A planted edge is recovered cleanly (*t* = 14.39, delta
+432.7 bp). **The detector works.** The real tape's near-zero count (4 loose / 0 strict)
is therefore a property of *how rare the pattern actually is*, not a bug or an
over-strict threshold. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support
of a real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Across 111 tickers and 4,957 name-years (up to 64.5 years of daily
  bars per name), the loose cut fires **4** times and the strict, literature-close cut
  fires **0** times — both below the pre-registered `MIN_N_FOR_TEST = 8`, so **no
  *t*-statistic is computed**. This is not "tested and found insignificant"; it is
  genuinely too rare to test on real data, even on the desk's largest single-pattern
  basket. A claim that cannot be exposed to disconfirming evidence at any practical
  sample size earns `NONE`, not `WEAK` — `WEAK` is reserved for a real, if fragile, point
  estimate, and there isn't one here.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is nothing to charge costs against. Even granting every
  benefit of the doubt to the four loose-cut hits, that is roughly **one signal every 15
  years pooled across 111 of the most liquid US equities** — no venue, no capacity, no
  book that can be built around it.
- **"Too rare to ever test on real markets?" — CONFIRMED.** The synthetic control proves
  the detector is unbiased (it finds planted patterns, stays quiet on nulls); the real
  tape proves the pattern itself essentially does not occur. The concealing baby swallow
  is less a trading signal than a museum piece.
